verdict.rationale: Open-sourcing is a fair question for a document-processing API platform, so the axis applies. However, nothing in the evidence shows Reducto's source code published under an open license. The published OpenAPI spec, llms.txt, CLI and MCP server docs are interface documentation, not source code under an open license, so they earn no credit.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license
